content:
Most SaaS companies ghost you once the check clears.

We have the opposite problem.

A customer recently asked us to stop calling them.

Not because of a sales pitch. But because we were checking their deployment health too often.

The team was monitoring the app. Proactively reaching out. Checking the pipes.

The customer finally told us: "We'll get back to you if we need anything."

It is a funny position to be in. Most vendors are invisible. We became the needy one.

But this happens because of how we build.

Most companies sell seats. They want you to log in.

We sell outcomes. We own the result, not just the software.

If the system fails, we fail. That is why we monitor. That is why we obsess over the deployment.

When you care about the outcome, it shows up in your behavior. Even if that behavior is slightly annoying.

We are now learning the art of being slightly less helpful.
